title: Machine-learning inference of stellar properties using integrated photometric and spectroscopic data
creator: Ilay Kamai, Alex M. Bronstein, Hagai B. Perets
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ilay Kamai, Alex M. Bronstein, Hagai B. Perets. Stellar astrophysics relies on diverse observational modalities—primarily photometric light curves and spectroscopic data—from which fundamental stellar properties are inferred. While machine learning (ML) has advanced analysis within individual modalities, the complementary information encoded across modalities remains largely underexploited. We present DESA (Dual Embedding model for Stellar Astrophysics), a novel multi-modal foundation model that integrates light curves and spectra to learn a unified, physically meaningful latent space for stars.

title: Entanglement and Purity in Open Systems: A Breakdown of the Lindblad Approach
creator: R. Serao, A. Quaranta, A. Capolupo, F. Franchini, S.M. Giampaolo
description: Abstract We examine the effectiveness of Lindblad master equation in capturing the short-time dynamics of entanglement and purity in open quantum systems. Focusing on two interacting two-level systems interacting with a larger environment, we compare the Lindbladian approach to a full microscopic treatment.

title: Unifying Chemical and Electrochemical Thermodynamics of Electrodes
creator: Archie Mingze Yao, Amal Sebastian, Venkatasubramanian Viswanathan
description: Abstract Batteries are critical for electrified transportation and aviation, yet thermodynamic understanding of electrode materials remains lacking, as indicated by the often-seen violation of the second law of thermodynamics of open-circuit voltage (OCV) models. On the other hand, thermodynamic modeling rarely utilizes electrochemical data such as OCV, entropic heat (dOCV/dT), which contains rich thermodynamic information.

title: Insights for Early Massive Black Hole Growth from JWST Detection of the [Ne v ] λ ​ 3427 \lambda 3427 Emission Line Journal: ApJL Facilities: JWST:NIRSpec
creator: Benny Trakhtenbrot, Claudio Ricci, Ezequiel Treister, Michael J. Koss, Richard Mushotzky, Kyuseok Oh, Alessandro Peca, Franz E. Bauer, Kriti Kamal Gupta, Tomer Reiss
description: Abstract We use the narrow [Ne v ] λ ​ 3427 \lambda 3427 emission line detected in the recently published JWST spectra of two galaxies, at z ≃ 6.9 z\simeq 6.9 and 5.6 5.6 , to study the key properties of the active galactic nuclei (AGN) and the supermassive black holes in their centers.

title: Roles of SN and AGN Feedback in Shaping the Baryonic Content in a Wide Range of Dark Matter Halo Mass
creator: Emanuele Contini, Changjo Seo, Jinsu Rhee, Seyoung Jeon, Sukyoung K. Yi
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Emanuele Contini, Changjo Seo, Jinsu Rhee, Seyoung Jeon, Sukyoung K. Yi. We build upon FEGA25 ( Contini et al. 2025 ) , a previously introduced semi-analytic model (SAM) for galaxy formation and evolution, by focusing on its enhanced treatment of supernova (SN) and active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback mechanisms.

title: Vision Language Action Models in Robotic Manipulation: A Systematic Review
creator: Muhayy Ud Din, Waseem Akram, Lyes Saad Saoud, Jan Rosell, Irfan Hussain*
description: Abstract Vision Language Action (VLA) models represent a transformative shift in robotics, with the aim of unifying visual perception, natural language understanding, and embodied control within a single learning framework. This review presents a comprehensive and forward-looking synthesis of the VLA paradigm, with a particular emphasis on robotic manipulation and instruction-driven autonomy.

title: Accretion from a Shock-Inflated Companion: Spinning Down Neutron Stars to Hour-Long Periods Journal: ApJ athena++ ( J. M. Stone et al. 2020 ) , numpy ( C. R. Harris et al. 2020 ) , scipy ( P. Virtanen et al. 2020 ) , matplotlib ( J. D. Hunter 2007 )
creator: Savannah Cary, Wenbin Lu, Calvin Leung, Tin Long Sunny Wong
description: Abstract Recent observations have unveiled a population of pulsars with spin periods of a few minutes to hours that lie beyond the traditional “death line.” If they originate from neutron stars (NSs), the existence of such ultra-long period pulsars (ULPs) challenges our current understanding of NS evolution and emission.

title: When CP requires θ ¯ = 0 \bar{\theta}=0 , not θ ¯ = π \bar{\theta}=\pi
creator: Luca Vecchi
description: Abstract Imposing CP or P forces the QCD topological angle to be either θ ¯ = 0 \bar{\theta}=0 or θ ¯ = π \bar{\theta}=\pi . However, only the former is phenomenologically viable. This implies that the assumption of CP or P alone cannot provide a framework for unambiguously solving the Strong CP problem.

title: Quasiparticle band picture bridging topology and strong correlations across energy scales
creator: Ivan Pasqua, Antonio Maria Tagliente, Gabriele Bellomia, Bartomeu Monserrat, Michele Fabrizio, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera
description: Abstract Understanding the interplay between electronic correlations and band topology remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics, primarily hindered by a language mismatch problem. While band topology is naturally formulated within a single-particle band theory, strong correlations typically elude such an effective one-body description.

title: Kernel Learning for Mean-Variance Trading Strategies
creator: Owen Futter, Nicola Muça Cirone, Blanka Horvath
description: Abstract In this article, we develop a kernel-based framework for constructing dynamic, path-dependent trading strategies under a mean-variance optimisation criterion. Building on the theoretical results of [ CS25 ] , we parameterise trading strategies as functions in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), enabling a flexible and non-Markovian approach to optimal portfolio problems.

title: Exotic superconducting states in altermagnets
creator: Kirill Parshukov, Andreas P. Schnyder
description: Abstract The interplay between magnetism and superconductivity is one of the central topics of condensed matter physics, which has recently been put into new light by the discovery of altermagnets. Here, we study this interplay from a fundamental symmetry perspective using irreducible co-representations of the altermagnetic spin-point groups.

title: Tracing Neutrino Non-Standard Interactions through Charged Lepton Collisions
creator: Sudip Jana, Saumyen Kundu, Santosh Kumar Rai
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sudip Jana, Saumyen Kundu, Santosh Kumar Rai. Neutrino non-standard interactions (NSI) play a crucial role in neutrino oscillations and can provide valuable insights for constructing models of neutrino masses and mixing. While NSI have been widely explored through oscillation and scattering experiments, as well as in cosmological and astrophysical contexts, we focus on probing them at future lepton colliders like the ILC, CLIC, and FCC- e ​ e ee .

title: Updated Bounds on the Minimal Left-Right Symmetric Model from LHC Dilepton Resonance Searches
creator: Gabriela Lichtenstein, Ricardo C. Silva, M. J. Neves, Farinaldo Queiroz
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gabriela Lichtenstein, Ricardo C. Silva, M. J. Neves, Farinaldo Queiroz. The Left-Right model is a popular extension of the Standard Model that features three new neutral gauge bosons, W R ± W^{\pm}_{R} and Z R Z_{R} .

title: Triangular solutions to a Riemann-Hilbert problem from superelliptic curves
creator: Anwar Al Ghabra 1 , Benjamin Piché 2 , Vasilisa Shramchenko 1
description: Abstract . We give fundamental solutions of arbitrarily sized matrix Fuchsian linear systems, in the case where the coefficients B ( i ) B^{(i)} of the systems are matrix solutions of the Schlesinger system that are upper triangular, and whose eigenvalues follow an arithmetic progression of a rational difference.

title: Exploring User Security and Privacy Attitudes and Concerns Toward the Use of General-Purpose LLM Chatbots for Mental Health
creator: Jabari Kwesi, Jiaxun Cao, Riya Manchanda, Pardis Emami-Naeini
description: Abstract Abstract Individuals are increasingly relying on large language model (LLM)-enabled conversational agents for emotional support. While prior research has examined privacy and security issues in chatbots specifically designed for mental health purposes, these chatbots are overwhelmingly “rule-based” offerings that do not leverage generative AI.

title: Natural super-orbitals representation of many-body operators
creator: Maxime Debertolis
description: Abstract We introduce the concept of natural super-orbitals for many-body operators, defined as the eigenvectors of the one-body super-density matrix associated with a vectorized operator. We first analyze the general analytical properties of these objects in various contexts, including the time-evolution operator of non-interacting Hamiltonians and Haar-random unitaries.

title: Grammatical Structure and Grammatical Variations in Non-Metric Iranian Classical Music
creator: Maziar Kanani School of Computer Science University of Galway Galway, Ireland m.kanani1@universityofgalway.ie Seán O’Leary School of Computer Science TU Dublin Dublin, Ireland sean.oleary@tudublin.ie James McDermott School of Computer Science University of Galway Galway, Ireland james.mcdermott@univ
description: Abstract In this study we introduce a symbolic dataset composed of non-metric Iranian classical music, and algorithms for structural parsing of this music, and generation of variations. The corpus comprises MIDI files and data sheets of Dastgah Shour from Radif Mirza Abdollah, the foundational repertoire of Iranian classical music.

title: Importance of gravitational effects on the performances of a fully passive oscillating-foil turbine deployed horizontally
description: Abstract This article presents a numerical study evaluating the impact of gravity on the performance of a fully passive oscillating-foil turbine operating in a horizontal configuration, that is, where the gravity acts along the heave direction. The study examines two sets of parameters corresponding to turbines driven by different aeroelastic instabilities.

title: Vanishing Metric Commutation Relation and Higher-derivative De Donder Gauge in Quadratic Gravity
creator: Ichiro Oda Department of Physics, Faculty of Science, University of the Ryukyus, Nishihara, Okinawa 903-0213, Japan
description: Abstract We show that the equal-time commutation relations (ETCRs) among the time derivatives of the metric tensor identically vanish in the higher-derivative de Donder gauge as well as the conventional de Donder gauge (or harmonic gauge) for general coordinate invariance in the manifestly covariant canonical operator formalism of quadratic gravity.

title: Pinning models with contact number constraint: the effect of disorder
creator: Giambattista Giacomin and Marco Zamparo
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Giambattista Giacomin and Marco Zamparo. Disordered pinning models are statistical mechanics models built on discrete renewal processes: renewal epochs in this context are called contacts . It is well known that pinning models can undergo a localization/delocalization phase transition: in the localized phase the typical density of contacts is positive and the largest gap between contacts is at most of the order of the logarithm of the size n n of the system, whereas the system is void of contacts in the delocalized phase.

title: Neural Network-Augmented Pfaffian Wave-functions for Scalable Simulations of Interacting Fermions
creator: Ao Chen, Zhou-Quan Wan, Anirvan Sengupta, Antoine Georges, Christopher Roth
description: Abstract Developing accurate numerical methods for strongly interacting fermions is crucial for improving our understanding of various quantum many-body phenomena, especially unconventional superconductivity. Recently, neural quantum states have emerged as a promising approach for studying correlated fermions, highlighted by the hidden fermion and backflow methods, which use neural networks to model corrections to fermionic quasiparticle orbitals.

title: Spin and valley-dependent tunneling in MoS 2 through magnetic barrier
creator: Ahmed Jellal, Nadia Benlakhouy, Pablo Díaz, David Laroze
description: Abstract We study electron transport in monolayer molybdenum disulfide MoS 2 subjected to a magnetic barrier. Our analysis employs a full-band continuum model to capture the relevant physical phenomena. We focus on how electron energy, magnetic field strength, and the geometric characteristics of the barrier affect the transmission and conductance.

title: Distributionally Robust Optimization with Adversarial Data Contamination Thanks: Supported in part by AFOSR Awards FA9550-21-1-0084 and FA9550-24-1-0076, the U.S. Office of Naval Research under award number N00014-22-1-2348, and by NSF CAREER Award CCF-2440563.
creator: Shuyao Li, Ilias Diakonikolas, Jelena Diakonikolas
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shuyao Li, Ilias Diakonikolas, Jelena Diakonikolas. Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) provides a framework for decision-making under distributional uncertainty, yet its effectiveness can be compromised by outliers in the training data. This paper introduces a principled approach to simultaneously address both challenges. We focus on optimizing Wasserstein-1 DRO objectives for generalized linear models with convex Lipschitz loss functions, where an ϵ \epsilon -fraction of the training data is adversarially corrupted.

title: Nonlinear Evolution of the Unstratified Polydisperse Dust Settling Instability
creator: Hossam Aly ,, Sijme-Jan Paardekooper
description: Abstract Context. The Dust Settling Instabilty (DSI) is a member of the Resonant Drag Instabilities (RDI) family, and is thus related to the Streaming Instability (SI). Linear calculations found that the unstratified monodisperse DSI has growth rates much higher than the SI even with lower initial dust to gas ratios.

title: Bridging Brains and Machines: A Unified Frontier in Neuroscience, Artificial Intelligence, and Neuromorphic Systems
creator: Sohan Shankar, Yi Pan, Hanqi Jiang, Zhengliang Liu, Mohammad R. Darbandi, Agustin Lorenzo, Junhao Chen, Md Mehedi Hasan, Arif Hassan Zidan, Eliana Gelman, Joshua A. Konfrst, Jillian Y. Russell, Katelyn Fernandes, Tianze Yang, Yiwei Li, Huaqin Zhao, Afrar Jahin, Triparna Ganguly, Shair Dinesha, Yifan
description: Abstract This position and survey paper identifies the emerging convergence of neuroscience, artificial general intelligence (AGI), and neuromorphic computing toward a unified research paradigm. Using a framework grounded in brain physiology, we highlight how synaptic plasticity, sparse spike-based communication, and multimodal association provide design principles for next-generation AGI systems that potentially combine both human and machine intelligences.

title: Interaction between skew-representability, tensor products, extension properties, and rank inequalities
creator: Kristóf Bérczi, Boglárka Gehér, András Imolay, László Lovász, Carles Padró, Tamás Schwarcz
description: Abstract Skew-representable matroids form a fundamental class in matroid theory, bridging combinatorics and linear algebra. They play an important role in areas such as coding theory, optimization, and combinatorial geometry, where linear structure is crucial for both theoretical insights and algorithmic applications.

title: Sensitivity of x-ray absorption at 5 ​ d 5d edges of high-valent light actinides to crystal-field strength and covalency effects
creator: J. Vegelius, D. K. Shuh, S. M. Butorin
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by J. Vegelius, D. K. Shuh, S. M. Butorin. The 5 ​ f 5f states were probed in ThO 2 and U(VI) and U(V) oxides using x-ray absorption spectroscopy at the actinide O 4 , 5 O_{4,5} edges. Measured data were analyzed by several approaches including atomic, crystal-field theory and the Anderson impurity model to take into account the hybridization of actinide valence states with oxygen 2 ​ p 2p states.

title: Extracting Document Relations from Search Corpus by Marginalizing over User Queries
creator: Yuki Iwamoto, Kaoru Tsunoda, Ken Kaneiwa, The University of Electro-Communications
description: Abstract Understanding relationships between documents in large-scale corpora is essential for knowledge discovery and information organization. However, existing approaches rely heavily on manual annotation or predefined relationship taxonomies. We propose EDR-MQ (Extracting Document Relations by Marginalizing over User Queries), a novel framework that discovers document relationships through query marginalization.

title: Toward Realistic Evaluations of Just-In-Time Vulnerability Prediction
creator: Duong Nguyen 1 , Thanh Le-Cong 2 , Triet Huynh Minh Le 3 , M. Ali Babar 3 , Quyet-Thang Huynh 1
description: Abstract Modern software systems are increasingly complex, presenting significant challenges in quality assurance. Just-in-time vulnerability prediction (JIT-VP) is a proactive approach to identifying vulnerable commits and providing early warnings about potential security risks. However, we observe that current JIT-VP evaluations rely on an idealized setting, where the evaluation datasets are artificially balanced, consisting exclusively of vulnerability-introducing and vulnerability-fixing commits.

title: 3S-Attack: Spatial, Spectral and Semantic Invisible Backdoor Attack Against DNN Models
creator: Jianyao Yin, Luca Arnaboldi, Honglong Chen, Pascal Berrang
description: Abstract Backdoor attacks involve either poisoning the training data or directly modifying the model in order to implant a hidden behavior, that causes the model to misclassify inputs when a specific trigger is present. During inference, the model maintains high accuracy on benign samples but misclassifies poisoned samples into an attacker-specified target class.

title: \pkg FARS: Factor Augmented Regression Scenarios in \proglang R
creator: Gian Pietro Bellocca Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, Ignacio Garrón Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, C. Vladimir Rodríguez-Caballero Department of Statistics, ITAM Department of Economics, Duke University, Esther Ruiz Universidad Carlos III de Madrid
description: Abstract \Plainauthor Gian Pietro Bellocca, Ignacio Garrón, Vladimir Rodríguez-Caballero, Esther Ruiz \Plaintitle fars: Factor Augmented Regression Scenarios in R \Shorttitle Factor Augmented Regression Scenarios in \proglang R \Abstract In the context of macroeconomic/financial time series, the \pkg FARS package provides a framework in \proglang R for the construction of conditional densities of the variable of interest based on the factor-augmented

title: Information Field Theory based Event Reconstruction for Cosmic Ray Radio Detectors
creator: Anna Nelles
description: Abstract Detection of extensive air showers with radio antennas is an appealing technique in cosmic ray physics. However, because of the high level of measurement noise, current reconstruction methods still leave room for improvement. Furthermore, reconstruction efforts typically focus only on a single aspect of the signal, such as the energy fluence or arrival time.

title: Revisiting the Abundance of Topological Materials
creator: Hossein Mirhosseini, Luis Elcoro, Andreas Knüpfer, Thomas D. Kühne
description: Abstract The classification of topological materials is revisited using advanced computational workflows that integrate hybrid density functional theory calculations with exact Hartree-Fock exchange. Unlike previous studies, our workflow optimizes atomic configurations obtained from the Materials Project Database, followed by precise electronic structure calculations.

title: Doc ⋆ : Access Control for Information-Theoretically Secure Key-Document Stores
creator: Yin Li, 1 Sharad Mehrota 2 , Shantanu Sharma 3 , and Komal Kumari 3
description: Abstract . This paper 1 1 1 An extended abstract of this version has been accepted in VLDB 2025. presents a novel key-based access control technique for secure outsourcing key-value stores where values correspond to documents that are indexed and accessed using keys. The proposed approach adopts Shamir’s secret-sharing that offers unconditional or information-theoretic security.

title: Parsing Musical Structure to Enable Meaningful Variations
creator: Maziar Kanani, Seán O’Leary, James McDermott
description: Abstract This paper presents a novel rule-based approach for generating music by varying existing tunes. We parse each tune to find the Pathway Assembly (PA) [ 1 ] , that is a structure representing all repetitions in the tune. The Sequitur algorithm [ 2 ] is used for this. The result is a grammar.

title: Eigenvalue Bounds for Symmetric Markov Chains on Multislices With Applications
creator: Prashanth Amireddy, Amik Raj Behera, Srikanth Srinivasan, Madhu Sudan
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Prashanth Amireddy, Amik Raj Behera, Srikanth Srinivasan, Madhu Sudan. We consider random walks on “balanced multislices” of any “grid” that respects the “symmetries” of the grid, and show that a broad class of such walks are good spectral expanders. (A grid is a set of points of the form 𝒮 n \mathcal{S}^{n} for finite 𝒮 \mathcal{S} , and a balanced multi-slice is the subset that contains an equal number of coordinates taking every value in 𝒮 \mathcal{S} .

title: Tunable magnon emission from a nano-optomagnet
creator: A. Duvakina, V. Karakhanyan, M. Xu, M. Suarez, A. J. M. Deenen, M. Raschetti, A. Mucchietto, T. Grosjean, D. Grundler
description: Abstract The growing demand for dense, energy-efficient, and high-frequency signal processing continues to drive device miniaturization. While downscaling remains a central challenge, magnons offer a promising solution as nanoscale signal carriers, supporting broadband operation from GHz to THz without moving charge carriers and generating Joule heating.

title: GenAI-Enabled Backlog Grooming in Agile Software Projects: An Empirical Study
creator: Kasper Lien Oftebro, Anh Nguyen-Duc, Kai-Kristian Kemell
description: Abstract Effective backlog management is critical for ensuring that development teams remain aligned with evolving requirements and stakeholder expectations. However, as product backlogs consistently grow in scale and complexity, they tend to become cluttered with redundant, outdated, or poorly defined tasks, complicating prioritization and decision-making processes.

title: A Benchmarking Framework for AI models in Automotive Aerodynamics
creator: Kaustubh Tangsali, Rishikesh Ranade, Mohammad Amin Nabian, Alexey Kamenev, Peter Sharpe, Neil Ashton, Ram Cherukuri, Sanjay Choudhry
description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a benchmarking framework within the open-source NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo-CFD framework designed to systematically assess the accuracy, performance, scalability, and generalization capabilities of AI models for automotive aerodynamics predictions. The open extensible framework enables incorporation of a diverse set of metrics relevant to the Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) community.

title: A molecular dynamics investigation of the dependence of mechanical properties of steel nanowires on C concentration. Journal: Journal of Computational Materials Science
creator: J.K. Liyanage, M.D.Nadeesha Tharundi, Laalitha S. I. Liyanage
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by J.K. Liyanage, M.D.Nadeesha Tharundi, Laalitha S. I. Liyanage. The temperature dependence of mechanical properties of steel nanowires with varying carbon content were studied using molecular dynamics simulations. Four interatomic potentials were assessed, with the Modified Embedded Atom Method (MEAM) potential developed by Liyanage et al. [ 1 ] selected for its accuracy in predicting the behavior of BCC Fe, FeC in the B 1 rock salt structure, and BCC iron with carbon.

title: RCG: Safety-Critical Scenario Generation for Robust Autonomous Driving via Real-World Crash Grounding
creator: Benjamin Stoler, Juliet Yang, Jonathan Francis, Jean Oh
description: Abstract Safety-critical scenarios are essential for training and evaluating autonomous driving (AD) systems, yet remain extremely rare in real-world driving datasets. To address this, we propose Real-world Crash Grounding (RCG), a scenario generation framework that integrates crash-informed semantics into adversarial perturbation pipelines.

title: Ground-Compose-Reinforce: Tasking Reinforcement Learning Agents through Formal Language
creator: Andrew C. Li, Toryn Q. Klassen, Andrew Wang, Parand A. Alamdari, Sheila A. McIlraithDepartment of Computer Science, University of TorontoVector Institute for Artificial Intelligence
description: Abstract Grounding language in complex perception (e.g. pixels) and action is a key challenge when building situated agents that can interact with humans via language. In past works, this is often solved via manual design of the language grounding or by curating massive datasets relating language to elements of the environment.

title: Ideal Boson Particle-Antiparticle System at Finite Temperatures
creator: D. Anchishkin, V. Gnatovskyy, I. Kondakova
description: Abstract The thermodynamic properties of an ideal bosonic system composed of particles and antiparticles at finite temperatures are examined within the framework of a scalar field model. It is assumed that particle-antiparticle pair creation occurs; however, the system is simultaneously subject to exact charge (isospin) conservation.

title: Auditing Facial Emotion Recognition Datasets for Posed Expressions and Racial Bias
creator: Rina Khan, Catherine Stinson
description: Abstract Facial expression recognition (FER) algorithms classify facial expressions into emotions such as happy, sad, or angry. An evaluative challenge facing FER algorithms is the fall in performance when detecting spontaneous expressions compared to posed expressions. An ethical (and evaluative) challenge facing FER algorithms is that they tend to perform poorly for people of some races and skin colors.

title: Search for Accelerator-Produced Sub-GeV Dark Matter with the NOvA Near Detector
creator: S. Abubakar, M. A. Acero, B. Acharya, P. Adamson, N. Anfimov, A. Antoshkin, E. Arrieta-Diaz, L. Asquith, A. Aurisano, A. Back, N. Balashov, P. Baldi, B. A. Bambah, E. F. Bannister, A. Barros, A. Bat, T. J. C. Bezerra, V. Bhatnagar, B. Bhuyan, J. Bian, A. C. Booth, R. Bowles, B. Brahma, C. Bromberg,
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by S. Abubakar, M. A. Acero, B. Acharya, P. Adamson, N. Anfimov, A. Antoshkin, E. Arrieta-Diaz, L. Asquith, A. Aurisano, A. Back, N. Balashov, P. Baldi, B. A. Bambah, E. F. Bannister, A. Barros, A. Bat, T. J. C. Bezerra, V. Bhatnagar, B. Bhuyan, J. Bian, A. C. Booth, R. Bowles, B. Brahma, C. Bromberg, . The NuMI facility at Fermilab produces a high-intensity beam of muon neutrinos and antineutrinos, designed to study neutrino oscillations.

title: IoT Malware Network Traffic Detection using Deep Learning and GraphSAGE Models
creator: Nikesh Prajapati 1 , Bimal Karki 2 , Saroj Gopali 2 , Akbar Siami Namin 2 Department of Computer Science 2 , Texas Tech University 2 nikeshprajapati7@gmail.com , { bimal.karki, saroj.gopali, akbar.namin }@ttu.edu
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nikesh Prajapati 1 , Bimal Karki 2 , Saroj Gopali 2 , Akbar Siami Namin 2 Department of Computer Science 2 , Texas Tech University 2 nikeshprajapati7@gmail.com , { bimal.karki, saroj.gopali, akbar.namin }@ttu.edu. This paper intends to detect IoT malicious attacks through deep learning models and demonstrates a comprehensive evaluation of the deep learning and graph-based models regarding malicious network traffic detection.

title: Detecting AI Assistance in Abstract Complex Tasks
creator: Tyler King, Nikolos Gurney, John H. Miller, Volkan Ustun
description: Abstract Detecting assistance from artificial intelligence is increasingly important as they become ubiquitous across complex tasks such as text generation, medical diagnosis, and autonomous driving. Aid detection is challenging for humans, especially when looking at abstract task data. Artificial neural networks excel at classification thanks to their ability to quickly learn from and process large amounts of data—assuming appropriate preprocessing.

title: Marginal Metals and Kosterlitz-Thouless Type Phase Transition in Disordered Altermagnets
creator: Chang-An Li, Bo Fu, Huaiming Guo, Björn Trauzettel, Song-Bo Zhang
description: Abstract Altermagnetism, a recently discovered magnetic phase characterized by spin-split bands without net magnetization, has emerged as promising platform for novel physics and potential applications. However, its stability against disorder—ubiquitous in real materials—remains poorly understood. Here, we study the electron localization properties of two-dimensional altermagnets subject to disorder.

title: The Surfaces of Small to Mid-Size Plutinos: Evidence of an Association Between Inclination and Surface Type Facilities: Magellan Baade (IMACS), CFHT (MegaPrime/MegaCam) TRIPPy, Source Extractor, SciPy
creator: Cameron Collyer, Rosemary E. Pike, Ying-Tung Chen (陳英同), Mike Alexandersen, Mark Comte, Samantha M. Lawler, Bryan J. Holler, J. J. Kavelaars, Lowell Peltier
description: Abstract Being one of the most populated mean motion resonances (MMR) with Neptune and lying close to the inner boundary of the present day cold classical disk, observations of the orbital and surface class distributions of the plutinos in the 3:2 MMR provide constraints on Neptune’s migration and insight into the compositional structure of the pre-migration planetesimal disk.

title: Causal Discovery for Linear Non-Gaussian Models with Disjoint Cycles
creator: Mathias Drton, Marina Garrote-López, Niko Nikov, Elina Robeva, Y. Samuel Wang
description: Abstract The paradigm of linear structural equation modeling readily allows one to incorporate causal feedback loops in the model specification. These appear as directed cycles in the common graphical representation of the models. However, the presence of cycles entails difficulties such as the fact that models need no longer be characterized by conditional independence relations.

title: FPC-Net: Revisiting SuperPoint with Descriptor-Free Keypoint Detection via Feature Pyramids and Consistency-Based Implicit Matching
creator: Ionuţ Grigore, Călin-Adrian Popa, Claudiu Leoveanu-Condrei
description: Abstract The extraction and matching of interest points are fundamental to many geometric computer vision tasks. Traditionally, matching is performed by assigning descriptors to interest points and identifying correspondences based on descriptor similarity. This work introduces a technique where interest points are inherently associated during detection, eliminating the need for computing, storing, transmitting, or matching descriptors.

title: Applying Text Embedding Models for Efficient Analysis in Labeled Property Graphs
creator: Michal Podstawski
description: Abstract Labeled property graphs often contain rich textual attributes that can enhance analytical tasks when properly leveraged. This work explores the use of pretrained text embedding models to enable efficient semantic analysis in such graphs. By embedding textual node and edge properties, we support downstream tasks including node classification and relation prediction with improved contextual understanding.

title: A Practical Guide to using Pauli Path Simulators for Utility-Scale Quantum Experiments
creator: Hrant Gharibyan, Siddharth Hariprakash, Mohammed Zuhair Mullath, Vincent P. Su
description: Abstract In this this paper we present an inexpensive protocol to perform runtime and memory estimation for large-scale experiments with Pauli Path simulators (PPS). Additionally, we propose a conceptually simple solution for studying whether PPS can be used as a scientific discovery tool, rather than reproducing existing answers.

title: Theory of Mind and Self-Disclosure to CUIs Conference: ToMinHAI at CUI’2025: Theory of Mind in Human-CUI Interaction; July 8, 2025; Waterloo, ON, Canada
creator: Samuel Rhys Cox
description: Abstract . Self-disclosure is important to help us feel better, yet is often difficult. This difficulty can arise from how we think people are going to react to our self-disclosure. In this workshop paper, we briefly discuss self-disclosure to conversational user interfaces (CUIs) in relation to various social cues.

title: A New Dataset and Performance Benchmark for Real-time Spacecraft Segmentation in Onboard Flight Computers
creator: Jeffrey Joan Sam 1 , Janhavi Sathe 1 , Nikhil Chigali 1 , Naman Gupta 1 , Radhey Ruparel 1 , Yicheng Jiang 1 , Janmajay Singh 1 , James W. Berck 2 , and Arko Barman 3
description: Abstract Spacecraft deployed in outer space are routinely subjected to various forms of damage due to exposure to hazardous environments. In addition, there are significant risks to the subsequent process of in-space repairs through human extravehicular activity or robotic manipulation, incurring substantial operational costs. Recent developments in image segmentation could enable the development of reliable and cost-effective autonomous inspection systems.

title: Reasoning about Medical Triage Optimization with Logic Programming
creator: Jaikrishna Manojkumar Patil, Adam Chapman, Richard Knuszka, John Chapman, Paulo Shakarian
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jaikrishna Manojkumar Patil, Adam Chapman, Richard Knuszka, John Chapman, Paulo Shakarian. We present a logic programming framework that orchestrates multiple variants of an optimization problem and reasons about their results to support high-stakes medical decision-making. The logic programming layer coordinates the construction and evaluation of multiple optimization formulations, translating solutions into logical facts that support further symbolic reasoning and ensure efficient resource allocation—specifically targeting the “right patient, right platform, right escort, right time, right destination” principle.

title: Entanglement and magic on the light-front
creator: Sam Alterman, Peter J. Love
description: Abstract In the light-front (LF) formulation of quantum field theory (QFT), physics is formulated from the perspective of a massless observer necessarily traveling at the speed of light. The LF formulation provides an alternative computational approach to lattice gauge theory, and has recently been investigated as a future application of quantum computers.

title: Propensity score weighting across counterfactual worlds: longitudinal effects under positivity violations
creator: Alec McClean, Iván Díaz
description: Abstract When examining a contrast between two interventions, longitudinal causal inference studies frequently encounter positivity violations when one or both regimes are impossible to observe for some subjects. Existing weighting methods either assume positivity holds or produce effects that conflate interventions’ impacts on ultimate outcomes with their effects on intermediate treatments and covariates.

title: Towards a Closer Collaboration Between Practice and Research in Agile Software Development Workshop: A Summary and Research Agenda
creator: Michael Neumann, Eva-Maria Schön, Mali Senapathi, Maria Rauschenberger, Tiago Silva da Silva
description: Abstract Agile software development principles and values have been widely adopted across various industries, influencing products and services globally. Despite its increasing popularity, a significant gap remains between research and practical implementation. This paper presents the findings of the first international workshop designed to foster collaboration between research and practice in agile software development.

title: "Is it always watching? Is it always listening?" Exploring Contextual Privacy and Security Concerns Toward Domestic Social Robots
creator: Henry Bell, Jabari Kwesi, Hiba Laabadli, Pardis Emami-Naeini
description: Abstract Equipped with artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced sensing capabilities, social robots are gaining interest among consumers in the United States. These robots seem like a natural evolution of traditional smart home devices. However, their extensive data collection capabilities, anthropomorphic features, and capacity to interact with their environment make social robots a more significant security and privacy threat.

title: Can Multimodal Foundation Models Understand Schematic Diagrams? An Empirical Study on Information-Seeking QA over Scientific Papers
creator: Yilun Zhao, Chengye WangChuhan LiArman Cohan Yale NLP Lab
description: Abstract This paper introduces MISS-QA, the first benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the ability of models to interpret schematic diagrams within scientific literature. MISS-QA comprises 1,500 expert-annotated examples over 465 scientific papers. In this benchmark, models are tasked with interpreting schematic diagrams that illustrate research overviews and answering corresponding information-seeking questions based on the broader context of the paper.

title: Dissecting the NVIDIA Blackwell Architecture with Microbenchmarks
creator: Aaron Jarmusch, Nathan Graddon, Sunita Chandrasekaran
description: Abstract The rapid development in scientific research provides a need for more compute power, which is partly being solved by GPUs. This paper presents a microarchitectural analysis of the modern NVIDIA Blackwell architecture by studying GPU performance features with thought through microbenchmarks.

title: Generation of a scalar vortex in a rotational frame
creator: M. Bordag, D. N. Voskresensky
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by M. Bordag, D. N. Voskresensky. We consider generation from the vacuum of a scalar charged field in a rigidly rotating frame. Adding an external magnetic field opens the way to Bose condensation of the field. This phenomenon has been studied for external uniform magnetic field occupying the whole volume of the uniformly rotating cylindrical system of finite radius R R with a Dirichlet boundary condition imposed on it. Besides continuing this study, we consider the field formed by a flux tube of small radius.

creator: Asim H. Gazi*, Member, IEEE, Bhanu T. Gullapalli*
description: Abstract Timely decision making is critical to the effectiveness of mobile health (mHealth) interventions. At predefined timepoints called “decision points,” intelligent mHealth systems such as just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs) estimate an individual’s biobehavioral context from sensor or survey data and determine whether and how to intervene. For interventions targeting habitual behavior (e.g.

title: M ultilayer A rtificial B enchmark for C ommunity D etection ( mABCD )
creator: Łukasz Kraiński, Michał Czuba, Piotr Bródka, Paweł Prałat, Bogumił Kamiński, François Théberge
description: Abstract The A rtificial B enchmark for C ommunity D etection ( ABCD ) model is a random graph model with community structure and power-law distribution for both degrees and community sizes. The model generates graphs similar to the well-known LFR model but it is faster, more interpretable, and can be investigated analytically.

title: Probabilistic Modeling of Antibody Kinetics Post Infection and Vaccination: A Markov Chain Approach
creator: Rayanne A. Luke ⋅ \cdot Prajakta Bedekar ⋅ \cdot Lyndsey M. Muehling, Glenda Canderan ⋅ \cdot Yesun Lee ⋅ \cdot Wesley A. Cheng ⋅ \cdot Judith A. Woodfolk, Jeffrey M. Wilson ⋅ \cdot Pia S. Pannaraj ⋅ \cdot Anthony J. Kearsley
description: Abstract Understanding dynamics of antibody levels is crucial for characterizing time-dependent response to immune events: either infections or vaccinations. The sequence and timing of these events significantly influence antibody level changes. Despite extensive interest in the recent years and many experimental studies, the effect of immune event sequences on antibody levels is not well understood.

title: Probing vector- vs. scalar-mediator dark-matter scenarios in B → ( K , K ∗ ) ​ M X B\to(K,K^{*})M_{X} decays
creator: Alexander Berezhnoy a , Wolfgang Lucha b and Dmitri Melikhov a,c,d
description: Abstract Within the hypothesis of the dark-matter origin of the excess in B → K ​ M X B\to KM_{X} decays over the standard-model expectation, observed by Belle-II, we show that: (i) Scalar- and vector-mediator scenarios may be unambiguously discriminated by measuring the differential distributions in B → K ​ M X B\to KM_{X} and B → K ∗ ​

title: Impact of Cosmic Ray-driven Outflows on Lyman- α \alpha Emission in Cosmological Simulations
creator: Taysun Kimm, Julien Devriendt, Francesco Rodríguez Montero, Adrianne Slyz, Jérémy Blaizot, Harley Katz, Beomchan Koh, Hyunmi Song
description: Abstract Cosmic ray (CR) feedback has been proposed as a powerful mechanism for driving warm gas outflows in galaxies. We use cosmological magnetohydrodynamic simulations to investigate the impact of CR feedback on neutral hydrogen ( H I ) in a 10 11 ​ M ⊙ 10^{11}\,\mbox{$M_{\odot}$} dark matter halo at 2 < z < 4 2<z<4 .

title: Static or Temporal? Semantic Scene Simplification to Aid Wayfinding in Immersive Simulations of Bionic Vision DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation emai; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Human-
creator: Justin M. Kasowski, Apurv Varshney, Michael Beyeler
description: Abstract . Visual neuroprostheses ( bionic eyes ) aim to restore a rudimentary form of vision by translating camera input into patterns of electrical stimulation. To improve scene understanding under extreme resolution and bandwidth constraints, prior work has explored computer vision techniques such as semantic segmentation and depth estimation.

title: Contrastive-KAN: A Semi-Supervised Intrusion Detection Framework for Cybersecurity with scarce Labeled Data
creator: Mohammad Alikhani, Reza Kazemi
description: Abstract In the era of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, cybersecurity and intrusion detection systems are vital for the secure and reliable operation of IoT and IIoT environments. A key challenge in this domain is the scarcity of labeled cyberattack data, as most industrial systems operate under normal conditions.

title: Stream programs are monoid homomorphisms with state
creator: Tyler Hou, Michael Arntzenius, Max Willsey
description: Abstract . We define a broad class of deterministic stream functions and show they can be implemented as homomorphisms into a “state” monoid. The homomorphism laws are simpler than the conditions of previous semantic frameworks for stream program optimization, yet retain support for rich equational reasoning over expressive dataflow programs, including sequential composition, parallel composition, and feedback.

title: Geometric Optimization and IPA-Induced Dispersion Tuning in Solid-Core Photonic Crystal Fibers
creator: Zekeriya Mehmet Yuksel, Hasan Oguz, Ozgur Onder Karakilinc, Halil Berberoglu, Mirbek Turduev, Muzaffer Adak, Sevgi Ozdemir Kart
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zekeriya Mehmet Yuksel, Hasan Oguz, Ozgur Onder Karakilinc, Halil Berberoglu, Mirbek Turduev, Muzaffer Adak, Sevgi Ozdemir Kart. This study presents a comprehensive numerical investigation of solid-core photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) with circular and hexagonal cladding geometries, aiming to optimize key optical parameters for nonlinear photonics and environmental sensing applications.

title: Reporte de Vulnerabilidades en IIoT. Proyecto DEFENDER.
creator: Pedro Almansa Jiménez
description: Abstract 1 Introducción IIoT 1.1 Objetivos del Reporte El objetivo principal de este informe técnico es realizar un estudio exhaustivo sobre los dispositivos que operan en entornos del Internet Industrial de las Cosas (IIoT), describiendo los escenarios que caracterizan esta categoría y analizando las vulnerabilidades que comprometen su seguridad.

title: React to This (RTT): A Nonverbal Turing Test for Embodied AI
creator: Chuxuan Zhang, Yasaman Etesam, Angelica Lim
description: Abstract We propose an approach to test embodied AI agents for interaction awareness and believability, particularly in scenarios where humans push them to their limits. Turing introduced the Imitation Game as a way to explore the question: “Can machines think?” The Total Turing Test later expanded this concept beyond purely verbal communication, incorporating perceptual and physical interaction.

title: Versatile and Generalizable Manipulation via Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning with Grounded Object Detection
creator: Huiyi Wang & Colin Bellinger, Fahim Shahriar & Alireza Azimi & Gautham Vasan & Rupam Mahmood
description: Abstract General-purpose robotic manipulation, including reach and grasp, is essential for deployment into households and workspaces involving diverse and evolving tasks. Recent advances propose using large pre-trained models, such as Large Language Models and object detectors, to boost robotic perception in reinforcement learning.

title: How Robust are LLM-Generated Library Imports? An Empirical Study using Stack Overflow
creator: Jasmine Latendresse, SayedHassan Khatoonabadi, Emad Shihab
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jasmine Latendresse, SayedHassan Khatoonabadi, Emad Shihab. Software libraries are central to the functionality, security, and maintainability of modern code. As developers increasingly turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) to assist with programming tasks, understanding how these models recommend libraries is essential. In this paper, we conduct an empirical study of six state-of-the-art LLMs, both proprietary and open-source, by prompting them to solve real-world Python problems sourced from Stack Overflow.

title: Semantic Context for Tool Orchestration
creator: Robert Müller
description: Abstract This paper demonstrates that Semantic Context (SC), leveraging descriptive tool information, is a foundational component for robust tool orchestration. Our contributions are threefold. First, we provide a theoretical foundation using contextual bandits, introducing SC-LinUCB and proving it achieves lower regret and adapts favourably in dynamic action spaces.

title: Confinement in QCD: A Hybrid String Model with Vortex Corrections and Entanglement Entropy
creator: Fidele J. Twagirayezu
description: Abstract Confinement in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), binding quarks and gluons into hadrons, is characterized by a linear potential and the Wilson loop area law. We develop an analytical framework in SU(3) gauge theory, proposing a hybrid effective string model that integrates chromoelectric flux tubes with topological corrections from ℤ 3 \mathbb{Z}_{3} center vortices.

title: Past, Present and Future: Exploring Adaptive AI in Software Development Bots
creator: Omar Elsisi, Glaucia Melo
description: Abstract Conversational agents, such as chatbots and virtual assistants, have become essential in software development, boosting productivity, collaboration, and automating various tasks. This paper examines the role of adaptive AI-powered conversational agents in software development, highlighting their ability to offer dynamic, context-aware assistance to developers.

title: Supporting SENĆO T EN Language Documentation Efforts with Automatic Speech Recognition
creator: Mengzhe Geng Patrick Littell Aidan Pine PENÁĆ Marc Tessier Roland Kuhn
description: Abstract The SENĆO T EN language, spoken on the Saanich peninsula of southern Vancouver Island, is in the midst of vigorous language revitalization efforts to turn the tide of language loss as a result of colonial language policies. To support these on-the-ground efforts, the community is turning to digital technology.

title: AF-Xray : Visual Explanation and Resolution of Ambiguity in Legal Argumentation Frameworks Conference: 20th Intl. Conf. on AI and Law; June 16–20, 2025; Chicago, IL, USA ISBN: XXX
creator: Yilin Xia, Heng Zheng, Shawn Bowers, Bertram Ludäscher
description: Abstract 1. Introduction Abstract argumentation frameworks ( Dung 1995 ) offer well-established, formal approaches for representing and reasoning about case law ( Bench-Capon 2020 ) . Given an argument x in an argumentation framework (AF), it is easy to determine the status of x under skeptical reasoning, i.e.

title: Waterfilling at the Edge: Optimal Percentile Resource Allocation via Risk-Averse Reduction
creator: Gokberk Yaylali †, Ahmad Ali Khan ‡, Dionysis Kalogerias †
description: Abstract We address deterministic resource allocation in point-to-point multi-terminal AWGN channels without inter-terminal interference, with particular focus on optimizing quantile transmission rates for cell-edge terminal service. Classical utility-based approaches —such as minimum rate, sumrate, and proportional fairness— are either overconservative, or inappropriate, or do not provide a rigorous and/or interpretable foundation for fair rate optimization at the edge.

title: REAL-IoT: Characterizing GNN Intrusion Detection Robustness under Practical Adversarial Attack Conference: the 2025 ACM Internet Measurement Conference; October 28–31, 2025; Madison, WI CCS: Security and privacy Network security CCS: General and reference Evaluation CCS: Computing methodologies Cros
creator: Zhonghao Zhan, Huichi Zhou, Hamed Haddadi
description: Abstract . Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) are often evaluated on single datasets, limiting their ability to generalize under distribution drift. Furthermore, their adversarial robustness is typically assessed using synthetic perturbations that lack realism. This measurement gap leads to an overestimation of GNN-based NIDS resilience.

title: On the forts and related parameters of the hypercube graph
creator: Boris Brimkov, Thomas R. Cameron, Owen Grubbs
description: Abstract In 2018, forts were defined as non-empty subsets of vertices in a graph where no vertex outside the set has exactly one neighbor in the set. Forts have since been used to characterize zero forcing sets, model zero forcing as an integer program, and provide lower bounds on the zero forcing number.

title: Covering Complete Geometric Graphs by Monotone Paths
creator: Adrian Dumitrescu, János Pach, Morteza Saghafian
description: Abstract Given a set A A of n n points (vertices) in general position in the plane, the complete geometric graph K n ​ [ A ] K_{n}[A] consists of all ( n 2 ) {n\choose 2} segments (edges) between the elements of A A .

title: Offline Reinforcement Learning with Wasserstein Regularization via Optimal Transport Maps
creator: Motoki Omura, Yusuke Mukuta, Kazuki Ota, Takayuki Osa, Tatsuya Harada
description: Abstract Offline reinforcement learning (RL) aims to learn an optimal policy from a static dataset, making it particularly valuable in scenarios where data collection is costly, such as robotics. A major challenge in offline RL is distributional shift, where the learned policy deviates from the dataset distribution, potentially leading to unreliable out-of-distribution actions.

title: Sparse Fine-Tuning of Transformers for Generative Tasks
creator: Wei Chen, Jingxi Yu, Zichen Miao, Qiang Qiu
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wei Chen, Jingxi Yu, Zichen Miao, Qiang Qiu. Large pre-trained transformers have revolutionized artificial intelligence across various domains, and fine-tuning remains the dominant approach for adapting these models to downstream tasks due to the cost of training from scratch. However, in existing fine-tuning methods, the updated representations are formed as a dense combination of modified parameters, making it challenging to interpret their contributions and understand how the model adapts to new tasks.

title: PhreshPhish : A Real-World, High-Quality, Large-Scale Phishing Website Dataset and Benchmark
creator: Thomas Dalton, Hemanth Gowda, Girish Rao, Sachin Pargi
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Thomas Dalton, Hemanth Gowda, Girish Rao, Sachin Pargi. Phishing remains a pervasive and growing threat, inflicting heavy economic and reputational damage. While machine learning has been effective in real-time detection of phishing attacks, progress is hindered by lack of large, high-quality datasets and benchmarks. In addition to poor-quality due to challenges in data collection, existing datasets suffer from leakage and unrealistic base rates, leading to overly optimistic performance results.

title: Rotation Periods of Candidate Single Late-M Dwarfs in TESS Facilities: TESS ( Ricker et al. 2015 ) , Gaia ( Vallenari et al. 2023 ) numpy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , scipy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) , matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , pandas ( pandas development team 2020 ) , astropy ( Astropy Collaboration e
creator: Samantha Lambier, Stanimir Metchev, Paulo Miles-Páez, Leslie Moranta, Dakota Wolfe, Joelene Hales, Jeffrey Martinovic
description: Abstract Recent studies suggest that the angular momentum evolution of late-M and brown dwarfs differs from the well-known spin-down evolution of hotter stars. Characterizing the distribution of rotation periods of these objects in the solar neighborhood can help elucidate this evolutionary pathway just above, at, and below the hydrogen burning limit.

title: On differential smoothness of certain Artin-Schelter regular algebras of dimension 5 5

A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andrés Rubiano. This article investigates the differential smoothness of various five-dimensional Artin–Schelter regular algebras. By analyzing the relationship between the number of generators and the Gelfand–Kirillov dimension, we provide structural obstructions to differential smoothness in specific algebraic families. In particular, we prove that certain two- and four-generator AS-regular algebras of global dimension five fail to admit a differential calculus, while a five-generator graded Clifford algebra provides a contrasting positive example. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification

title: Higher spin Richardson-Gaudin model with time-dependent coupling: Exact dynamics
creator: Suvendu Barik, Lieuwe Bakker, Vladimir Gritsev, Jiří Minář, Emil A. Yuzbashyan
description: Abstract We determine the exact asymptotic many-body wavefunction of a spin- s s Richardson-Gaudin model with a coupling inversely proportional to time, for time evolution starting from the ground state at t = 0 + t=0^{+} and for arbitrary s s .

title: MultiVox : Benchmarking Voice Assistants for Multimodal Interactions
creator: Ramaneswaran Selvakumar, Ashish Seth, Nishit Anand
description: Abstract The rapid progress of Large Language Models (LLMs) has empowered omni models to act as voice assistants capable of understanding spoken dialogues. These models can process multimodal inputs beyond text, such as speech and visual data, enabling more context-aware interactions.

title: CHEX-MATE: Cluster Multi-Probes in Three Dimensions (CLUMP-3D)
creator: A. Gavidia, J. Kim, J. Sayers, M. Sereno, L. Chappuis, D. Eckert, K. Umetsu, H. Bourdin, F. De Luca, S. Ettori, M. Gaspari, R. Gavazzi, S. Kay, L. Lovisari, P. Mazzotta, G. W. Pratt, E. Rasia, M. Rossetti
description: Abstract Under the standard model of hierarchical structure formation, the overall geometry of galaxy clusters is better described by a triaxial ellipse than a sphere. As a result, applying spherically-symmetric models can result in significant biases, with masses derived from WL observations being particularly sensitive.

title: Probing Cosmic Neutrino Background through Parametric Fluorescence
creator: Guo-yuan Huang, Shun Zhou
description: Abstract We point out that relic neutrinos from the Big Bang may induce the parametric fluorescence in molecular systems, which offers a novel way to discover cosmic neutrino background. By coherently scattering with molecular energy levels, a massive neutrino can spontaneously “decay” into a lighter neutrino and an infrared signal photon, i.e.

title: Quorum sensing of light-activated colloids in nematic liquid crystals
creator: Antonio Tavera-Vázquez, David Martin, Haijie Ren, Sam Rubin, Andrés Córdoba, Rui Zhang, Vincenzo Vitelli, Juan J. de Pablo
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Antonio Tavera-Vázquez, David Martin, Haijie Ren, Sam Rubin, Andrés Córdoba, Rui Zhang, Vincenzo Vitelli, Juan J. de Pablo. Motile living organisms routinely probe their surroundings to adapt in ever-evolving environments. Although synthetic microswimmers offer surrogates for self-propelled living entities, they often lack the complex feedback mechanisms that enable organisms to adapt.

title: Focus on Texture: Rethinking Pre-training in Masked Autoencoders for Medical Image Classification
creator: Chetan Madan, Aarjav Satia *, Soumen Basu, Pankaj Gupta, Usha Dutta, Chetan Arora
description: Abstract Masked Autoencoders ( MAEs ) have emerged as a dominant strategy for self-supervised representation learning in natural images, where models are pre-trained to reconstruct masked patches with a pixel-wise mean squared error ( MSE ) between original and reconstructed RGB values as the loss.

title: Geodesics, Scalar Fields, and GUP-Corrected Thermodynamics of Charged BTZ-like Black Holes in Bopp-Podolsky Electrodynamics
description: Abstract In Ref. [ 1 ] , the spacetime geometry generated by compact objects in (2+1)-dimensional Bopp-Podolsky electrodynamics is derived. Using a perturbative approach, the authors derived a charged BTZ-like black hole solution and computed corrections up to second order in a perturbative expansion valid far from the horizon.

title: Domain-Adaptive Small Language Models for Structured Tax Code Prediction
creator: Souvik Nath, Sumit Wadhwa, Luis Perez
description: Abstract Every day, multinational firms process thousands of transactions, each of which must adhere to tax regulations that vary by jurisdiction and are often nuanced. The determination of product and service tax codes, such as HSN or SAC is a major use case in Tax compliance. An accurate determination of such codes is imperative to avoid any tax penalties.

title: Start from the End: A Framework for Computational Policy Exploration to Inform Effective and Geospatially Consistent Interventions applied to COVID-19 in St. Louis
creator: David O’Gara, Matt Kasman, Matthew D. Haslam, Ross A. Hammond
description: Abstract Mathematical models are a powerful tool to study infectious disease dynamics and intervention strategies against them in social systems. However, due to their detailed implementation and steep computational requirements, practitioners and stakeholders are typically only able to explore a small subset of all possible intervention scenarios, a severe limitation when preparing for disease outbreaks.

title: Learning from Imperfect Data: Robust Inference of Dynamic Systems using Simulation-based Generative Model
creator: Hyunwoo Cho, Hyeontae Jo, Hyung Ju Hwang
description: Abstract System inference for nonlinear dynamic models, represented by ordinary differential equations (ODEs), remains a significant challenge in many fields, particularly when the data are noisy, sparse, or partially observable. In this paper, we propose a Simulation-based Generative Model for Imperfect Data (SiGMoID) that enables precise and robust inference for dynamic systems.

title: Evaluating Generated Commit Messages with Large Language Models Conference: The 48th International Conference on Software Engineering; April 12–18, 2026; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil Conference: 48th International Conference on Software Engineering; April 12–18, 2026; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil 48th Internati
creator: Qunhong Zeng, Yuxia Zhang, Zexiong Ma, Bo Jiang, Ningyuan Sun, Klaas-Jan Stol, Xingyu Mou, Hui Liu
description: Abstract . Commit messages are essential in software development as they serve to document and explain code changes. Yet, their quality often falls short in practice, with studies showing significant proportions of empty or inadequate messages. While automated commit message generation has advanced significantly, particularly with Large Language Models (LLMs), the evaluation of generated messages remains challenging.

title: LLMATCH: a Unified Schema Matching Framework with Large Language Models Thanks: Supported by the Singapore Ministry of Education Academic Research Fund Tier 1 grant (23-SIS-SMU-063) and the SMU-SUTD Internal Research Grant Call (SMU-SUTD 2023_02_01)
creator: Sha Wang, Yuchen Li, Hanhua Xiao, Bing Tian Dai, Roy Ka-Wei Lee, Yanfei Dong, Lambert Deng
description: Abstract Schema matching is a foundational task in enterprise data integration, aiming to align disparate data sources. While traditional methods handle simple one-to-one table mappings, they often struggle with complex multi-table schema matching in real-world applications. We present LLMatch , a unified and modular schema matching framework.

title: Omnisoot: an object-oriented process design package for gas-phase synthesis of carbonaceous nanoparticles
creator: Mohammad Adib, Sina Kazemi, M. Reza Kholghy
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mohammad Adib, Sina Kazemi, M. Reza Kholghy. A computational tool, Omnisoot, was developed utilizing the chemical kinetics capabilities of Cantera to model the formation of carbonaceous nanoparticles, such as soot and Carbon Black (CB), from the reactions of gaseous hydrocarbons. Omnisoot integrates constant volume, constant pressure, perfectly stirred, and plug flow reactor models with four inception models from the literature, as well as two population balance models: a monodisperse model and a sectional model.

title: LLMs on Trial: Evaluating Judicial Fairness for Large Language Models
creator: Yiran Hu, Zongyue Xue, Haitao Li, Siyuan Zheng, Qingjing Chen, Shaochun Wang, Xihan Zhang, Ning Zheng, Yun Liu, Qingyao Ai, Yiqun Liu, Charles L.A. Clarke, & Weixing Shen
description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in high-stakes fields where their decisions impact rights and equity. However, LLMs’ judicial fairness and implications for social justice remain underexplored. When LLMs act as judges, the ability to fairly resolve judicial issues is a prerequisite to ensure their trustworthiness.

title: Orders of commutators and Products of conjugacy classes in finite groups

We prove that the commutator [ x , g ] [x,g] is a p p -element for every g ∈ G g\in G if and only if x x is central modulo O p ​ ( G ) , O_{p}(G), where O p ​ ( G ) O_{p}(G) denotes the largest normal p p -subgroup of G G .

creator: Zibin Zhao 1, Guilong Li 1, Huanbo Luo 1,2, Bin Liu 1,3, Gui-hua Chen 4, Boris A. Malomed 5,6, Yongyao Li 1,3
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zibin Zhao 1, Guilong Li 1, Huanbo Luo 1,2, Bin Liu 1,3, Gui-hua Chen 4, Boris A. Malomed 5,6, Yongyao Li 1,3. Hopfions are a class of three-dimensional (3D) solitons which are built as vortex tori carrying intrinsic twist of the toroidal core.

title: Cappell-Shaneson polynomials
creator: Hisaaki Endo, Kazunori Iwaki, Andrei Pajitnov
description: Abstract . In the seminal work [ 7 ] S. Cappell and J. Shaneson constructed a pair of inequivalent embeddings of ( n − 1 ) (n-1) -spheres in homotopy ( n + 1 ) (n+1) -spheres for every square matrix of order n n with special properties (a Cappell-Shaneson matrix).

title: HanjaBridge: Resolving Semantic Ambiguity in Korean LLMs via Hanja-Augmented Pre-Training
creator: Seungho Choi
description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) often show poor performance in low-resource languages like Korean, partly due to unique linguistic challenges such as homophonous Sino-Korean words that are indistinguishable in Hangul script. To address this semantic ambiguity, we propose HanjaBridge, a novel meaning-injection technique integrated into a continual pre-training (CPT) framework.

title: A Learning Framework For Cooperative Collision Avoidance of UAV Swarms Leveraging Domain Knowledge
creator: Shuangyao Huang, Haibo Zhang, Zhiyi Huang
description: Abstract This paper presents a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for cooperative collision avoidance of UAV swarms leveraging domain knowledge-driven reward. The reward is derived from knowledge in the domain of image processing, approximating contours on a two-dimensional field. By modeling obstacles as maxima on the field, collisions are inherently avoided as contours never go through peaks or intersect.

title: Quantifying the Active Galactic Nuclei Fraction in Cosmic Voids via Mid-Infrared Variability
creator: Anish S. Aradhey, Anca Constantin, Michael S. Vogeley, Kelly A. Douglass
description: Abstract Observations and theoretical simulations suggest that the large scale environment plays a significant role in how galaxies form and evolve and, in particular, whether and when galaxies host an actively accreting supermassive black hole in their center (i.e., an Active Galactic Nucleus, or AGN).

title: Frequency comb in twisted magnonic crystals
creator: Minghao Li, Zhejunyu Jin, Zhaozhuo Zeng, Peng Yan
description: Abstract While twisted magnonic crystals (MCs) have recently gained attention for their intriguing linear phenomena, such as magnon flat bands, their nonlinear dynamics—particularly the generation of magnonic frequency combs (MFCs)—have remained largely unexplored. In this work, we demonstrate the creation of MFCs in twisted MCs using two-tone microwave excitation.

title: Modelling the interaction between ethnicity and infectious disease transmission dynamics
creator: Vincent X. Lomas ab , and Tim Chambers b , Michael J. Plank a
description: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, Aotearoa followed an elimination strategy followed by a mitigation strategy, which saw high success and kept health impact low. However, there were inequities in health outcomes, notably that Māori and Pacific Peoples had lower vaccine coverage and experienced higher age-standardised rates of hospitalisation and death.

title: A short proof of the existence of the injective envelope of an operator space
creator: Thomas Sinclair
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Thomas Sinclair. We use Ellis’ lemma to give a simple proof of the existence of the injective envelope of an operator space first shown by work of Hamana and Ruan. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 46L07, 46L55, 22A20 Ramsey-theoretic methods provide powerful tools in functional analysis, ergodic theory, and additive combinatorics: see [ 1 , 9 , 16 ] for many of these applications.

title: Polarons in two-dimensional polar materials: All-coupling variational theory
creator: A. Kudlis, V. Shahnazaryan, I. V. Tokatly
description: Abstract We present a detailed and self-contained theoretical study of polarons in two-dimensional (2D) polar materials, which extends the classical macroscopic theory of Fröhlich polarons to the 2D case. The theory is fully determined by experimentally accessible parameters, the static and optical 2D polarizabilities of a monolayer, the frequency of transverse optical phonons, and the effective mass of charge carriers.

title: Demonstration of a 1820 channel multiplexer for transition-edge sensor bolometers
creator: J.C. Groh, Z. Ahmed, J. Austermann, J. Beall, D. Daniel, S.M. Duff, S.W. Henderson, J. Hubmayr, R. Lew, M. Link, T.J. Lucas, J.A.B. Mates, M. Silva-Feaver, R. Singh, J. Ullom, L. Vale, J. Van Lanen, M. Vissers, C. Yu
description: Abstract The scalability of most transition-edge sensor arrays is limited by the multiplexing technology which combines their signals over a reduced number of wires and amplifiers. In this letter, we present and demonstrate a multiplexer design optimized for transition-edge sensor bolometers with 1820 sensors per readout unit, a factor of two larger than the previous state-of-the-art.

title: The model theory of metric lattices: pseudofinite partition lattices
creator: José Contreras Mantilla, Thomas Sinclair
description: Abstract . We initiate the study of general metric lattices in the context of the model theory of metric structures. As an application we develop a theory of pseudo-finite limits of partition lattices and connect this theory with the theory of continuous limits of partition lattices due to Björner and Lovász.

title: Towards a Utility-Scale Quantum Edge Detection for Real-World Medical Image Data Thanks: This research was sponsored by the Richard T. Cheng Endowment, Old Dominion University.
creator: Emmanuel Billias, Nikos Chrisochoides
description: Abstract We present a two-level decomposition strategy to enhance the quality and performance of Quantum Hadamard Edge Detection (QHED) for practical image analysis on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices. A Data-Level Decomposition partitions an input image into P augmented sub-images, each encoded into a separate quantum circuit.

title: Scalable Variational Inference for Multinomial Probit Models under Large Choice Sets and Sample Sizes
creator: Gyeongjun Kim, Yeseul Kang, Lucas Kock, Prateek Bansal, Keemin Sohn
description: Abstract The multinomial probit (MNP) model is widely used to analyze categorical outcomes due to its ability to capture flexible substitution patterns among alternatives. Conventional likelihood-based and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) estimators become computationally prohibitive in high-dimensional choice settings.

title: Biological Processing Units: Leveraging an Insect Connectome to Pioneer Biofidelic Neural Architectures
creator: Siyu Yu, Zihan Qin, [-1ex] Tingshan Liu, Beiya Xu, [0.15ex] R. Jacob Vogelstein, Jason Brown, [0.15ex] Joshua T. Vogelstein
description: Abstract The complete connectome of the Drosophila larva brain offers a unique opportunity to investigate whether biologically evolved circuits can support artificial intelligence. We convert this wiring diagram into a Biological Processing Unit (BPU)—a fixed recurrent network derived directly from synaptic connectivity.

title: Solving Linear Programs with Differential Privacy
creator: Alina Ene, Huy L. Nguyen, Ta Duy Nguyen, Adrian Vladu
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alina Ene, Huy L. Nguyen, Ta Duy Nguyen, Adrian Vladu. We study the problem of solving linear programs of the form A ​ x ≤ b Ax\leq b , x ≥ 0 x\geq 0 with differential privacy.

title: Effect of Galactic Chemical Evolution on Exoplanet Properties Facilities: UNLV, Cherry Creek Magrathea ( Huang et al. 2022 ) , NumPy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 )
creator: Jason H. Steffen, Cody Shakespeare, Robert Royer, David Rice, Allona Vazan
description: Abstract We couple a simplified model for the galactic chemical evolution, with software that models the condensation of dust in protoplanetary disks and software that models the interior structure of planets in order to estimate the effects that the galactic chemical evolution has on the properties of planets as they form over time.

title: LATIS: A Sample of IGM-Selected Protoclusters and Protogroups at z ∼ 2.5 z\sim 2.5
creator: Andrew B. Newman, Mahdi Qezlou, Gwen C. Rudie, Nima Chartab, Guillermo A. Blanc, Daniel D. Kelson, Simeon Bird, Caitlin Casey, Enrico Congiu, Olga Cucciati, Denise Hung, Brian C. Lemaux, Victoria Pérez, Jorge Zavala
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andrew B. Newman, Mahdi Qezlou, Gwen C. Rudie, Nima Chartab, Guillermo A. Blanc, Daniel D. Kelson, Simeon Bird, Caitlin Casey, Enrico Congiu, Olga Cucciati, Denise Hung, Brian C. Lemaux, Victoria Pérez, Jorge Zavala. The Ly α \alpha Tomography IMACS Survey (LATIS) has produced large 3D maps of the intergalactic medium (IGM), providing a new window on the cosmic web at z ∼ 2.5 z\sim 2.5 .

title: LATIS: Comparing Galaxy and IGM Tomography Maps as Tracers of Large-Scale Structure and Protoclusters at z ∼ 2.5 z\sim 2.5
creator: Andrew B. Newman, Nima Chartab, Mahdi Qezlou, Gwen C. Rudie, Guillermo A. Blanc, Daniel D. Kelson, Simeon Bird, Caitlin Casey, Enrico Congiu, Olga Cucciati, Denise Hung, Brian C. Lemaux, Victoria Pérez, Jorge Zavala
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andrew B. Newman, Nima Chartab, Mahdi Qezlou, Gwen C. Rudie, Guillermo A. Blanc, Daniel D. Kelson, Simeon Bird, Caitlin Casey, Enrico Congiu, Olga Cucciati, Denise Hung, Brian C. Lemaux, Victoria Pérez, Jorge Zavala. We investigate the consistency of intergalactic medium (IGM) tomography and galaxy surveys as tracers of the cosmic web and protoclusters at z ∼ 2.5 z\sim 2.5 .

title: Modeling Understanding of Story-Based Analogies Using Large Language Models
creator: Kalit Inani*, Keshav Kabra*, Vijay Marupudi, Sashank Varma
description: Abstract Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have brought them closer to matching human cognition across a variety of tasks. How well do these models align with human performance in detecting and mapping analogies? Prior research has shown that LLMs can extract similarities from analogy problems but lack robust human-like reasoning. Building on Webb et al.

title: Whom to Respond To? A Transformer-Based Model for Multi-Party Social Robot Interaction
creator: He Zhu, Ryo Miyoshi, Yuki Okafuji
description: Abstract Prior human-robot interaction (HRI) research has primarily focused on single-user interactions, where robots do not need to consider the timing or recipient of their responses. However, in multi-party interactions, such as at malls and hospitals, social robots must understand the context and decide both when and to whom they should respond.

title: Extension of a complete monotonicity theorem with applications. Thanks: This paper is in final form and no version of it will be submitted for publication elsewhere.

description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhen-Hang-Yang.
